title: The entanglement-assisted transmission capacity is a strong converse bound for identification
summary: Classical identification via a noisy channel is a communication task in which the receiver is not required to reconstruct the full transmitted message, but only to decide whether it coincides with a message of interest. This relaxation allows the number of identifiable messages to grow doubly exponentially with the blocklength. For quantum channels, the resulting (doubly exponential) identification capacity $C_{\mathrm{ID}}$ can strictly exceed the ordinary (exponential) transmission capacity $C$.
